messages:
maria: Heads-up — deploy-bot flagged a post-canary tail latency regression for release v3.6.0. Some Dedicated routes may be affected. Comments?

deploy-bot: Alert: p95 > 480ms for 4m on canary slice. Error spike: 502s observed. Recommended: automatic revert to v3.5.2 (policy).

li: Quick check of canary logs points to repeated kvcache misses and a quantization fallback path. Kernel path looks different than previous builds.

devin: If autorevert runs it'll affect all slices. Can we suppress auto and do a surgical rollback on canary only? That keeps Dedicated customers stable.

ops-bot: @maria hold placed: suppressing auto-rollback for 10 minutes per operator request. Please escalate if metrics worsen.

maria: Agree with holding. Plan proposal: 1) rollback canary slice to previous stable; 2) pin Dedicated routes to last stable; 3) notify CS/AE; 4) triage offline.

devin: I can execute the canary rollback and the route pin. Commands I will run: 
```
# rollback canary slice to stable
redwoodctl rollout rollback --service=inference --to-version=3.5.2 --target=canary --reason="post-canary p95"
# pin Dedicated route to stable
redwoodctl routes pin --route=dedicated-usw2 --version=3.5.2 --note="auto-protect-dedicated"
```

li: Sharing a short log excerpt that matches the telemetry:
```
[2026-04-01T09:14:08Z] frontend: upstream 10.2.9.8:502 Bad Gateway
[2026-04-01T09:14:09Z] runtime: kvcache miss -> quant fallback -> latency 712ms
[2026-04-01T09:14:09Z] kernel-select: path switched to fallback-int8
```

devin: Starting canary rollback now.

ops-bot: ACTION: devin initiated rollback at 2026-04-01T09:16:22Z. Job id: job-rollback-4631234567-1

devin: Rollback finished on canary. Running smoke and short traffic validation.

devin: Validation: p95 = 130ms on canary, 502 errors cleared from canary logs.

maria: Verified dashboards look normal. Thanks devin. CS/AE note drafted below, sending now: 

"Customer brief: During a canary deployment for release v3.6.0 we detected increased tail latency for a small subset of traffic. We have reverted the canary to the prior stable version and pinned Dedicated routes as a precaution. No action is required on your side; were investigating and will follow up with details and a timeline for re-release."

li: Next steps for eng: gather runtime/kernel selection traces, test with/without the quant flag, and reproduce locally. Open a post-mortem ticket and include rollback commands and timelines.

maria: Also update the release notes to mark v3.6.0 as paused and reference the rollback. Reattempt only after a validated fix in a follow-up window.

devin: Post-mortem ticket opened: PM-12345. Attaching logs and commands. Will hold the canary pin for 45 minutes then release back to deploybot for retry scheduling.

deploy-bot: Recorded manual rollback and pins. Recommendation: revert recent kernel selector change in next build candidate.

maria: Closing this thread for the immediate incident. If anything else pops up, revive here or @ops. :white_check_mark:
